facts.statement: The holotype specimen is a partially articulated skeleton of an 8-year-old subadult.
facts.quote: The holotype of Bannykus wulatensis is IVPP V25026, a partially-articulated incomplete skeleton of an 8 year old subadult.

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered in 2009 and displayed in Japan in 2012 under the unofficial name Wulatesaurus.
facts.quote: It was discovered in 2009 and in 2012, its remains were displayed in Japan under the unofficial name "Wulatesaurus".

facts.statement: The species was formally named Bannykus wulatensis in 2018.
facts.quote: It was given the binomial name Bannykus wulatensis in 2018

facts.statement: The immature holotype was estimated to be 2.77 meters long and weigh between 24 and 30 kg.
facts.quote: Bannykus is large for an alvarezsaurian theropod, with an estimated length of 2.77 m and body mass of approximately 24 - 30 kg for the immature holotype.

facts.statement: Analysis in 2025 of the holotype's intestinal contents detected bone-derived material, suggesting a carnivorous diet.
facts.quote: In 2025, Wang and colleagues identified hard tissue debris and possible soft tissues in the intestinal contents of the holotype (represented by the yellowish conglomerate) based on scanning electron microscopy, which was consistent with further Raman spectroscopy analysis that detected "characteristic peaks indicative of bone-derived material", suggesting that Bannykus probably had a carnivorous diet.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the forelimbs were capable of generalized motions used for various digging styles.
facts.quote: The forelimbs of Bannykus were biomechanically capable of generalised motions, and the animal likely used them for a variety of digging styles.

facts.statement: The animal lived during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous,

facts.statement: The genus Bannykus is monotypic, containing only the species Bannykus wulatensis.
facts.quote: It includes one species, Bannykus wulatensis.

facts.statement: The species was found in the Bayin-Gobi Formation of Inner Mongolia, China.
facts.quote: Bannykus is an extinct monotypic genus of alvarezsauroid from the Early Cretaceous Bayin-Gobi Formation of Inner Mongolia, China.

facts.statement: Bannykus fills a 70-million-year evolutionary gap by showing intermediate features between early and late alvarezsaurids.
facts.quote: Bannykus, along with Xiyunykus, fills a 70-million year gap in alvarezsaur evolution by exhibiting morphologies intermediate between the typical theropod forelimb of Haplocheirus and the highly reduced forelimbs and minute teeth of Late Cretaceous alvarezsaurids.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis confirms a basal position for Alvarezsauria within Maniraptora.
facts.quote: El análisis confirma una posición basal de Alvarezsauria dentro de Maniraptora.

facts.statement: Analysis shows that alvarezsaurian evolution was modular, with forelimbs modifying before hindlimbs.
facts.quote: El análisis también muestra que la evolución de los alvarezsaurianos fue modular. Las partes delanteras del esqueleto se modificaron antes que las partes posteriores.

facts.statement: Bannykus bridges the gap between early alvarezsaurians with long grasping arms and later forms with highly specialized short forelimbs and a single claw.
facts.quote: Bannykus, junto con el descrito simultáneamente Xiyunykus cierran una brecha importante en la evolución de Alvarezsauria, los géneros más antiguos, como el Haplocheirus del Jurásico Superior, tienen brazos largos con garras adecuadas para agarrar. Los géneros posteriores del Cretácico superior, sin embargo, tienen extremidades anteriores más especializadas, que son más cortas y tienen una sola garra.

facts.statement: The forelimb of Bannykus is shorter than Jurassic alvarezsaurians but longer than Late Cretaceous alvarezsaurids.
facts.quote: El antebrazo de Bannykus más corto que el de los alvarezsaurianos del Jurásico superior, pero más largo que el de alvarezsáuridos del Cretácico superior.

facts.statement: The forelimbs have an extended thumb and shortened other digits, indicating a loss of grasping function.
facts.quote: Los antebrazos tienen un pulgar extendido, mientras que todos los otros dedos se acortan, lo que indica que ya han perdido la función de agarre.

facts.statement: The species lived between 124 and 113 million years ago during the Barremian stage in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Bannykus wulatensis (zh. "Media garra del condado de Wulatehouqi") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Bannykus de dinosaurio terópodo alvarezsauroideo que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, entre el 124 a 113 millones de años, durante el Barremiense en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil was found in the Bayin Gobi Formation in Inner Mongolia, China.
facts.quote: El material fósil del holotipo de B. wulatensis se encontró en la formación Bayin Gobi , que se encuentra en Mongolia Interior, China.

facts.statement: Bannykus originates from Asia, suggesting the group evolved there before spreading to other continents.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto Bannykus proviene como todos los demás conocido alvarezsáuridos del Jurásico y el Cretácico Superior o Inferior de Asia, lo que sugiere la conclusión de que el grupo tuvo su origen allí.

facts.statement: It is debated whether alvarezsaurian species appeared on other continents via migration or allopatric speciation, with recent analysis favoring migration.
facts.quote: Según un análisis filogenético, la aparición de especies de Alvarezsauria en otros continentes es el resultado de la propagación en lugar de la especiación alopátrica como se sospechó anteriormente.

facts.statement: The time range is recorded as Aptian to Aptian, from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The name Bannykus refers to the transitional characteristics seen in this theropod.
rejected.quote: This refers to the transitional characteristics seen in this theropod.
